title: Common & Useful SAP Transaction Codes (TCodes)
description: This manual outlines frequently used SAP TCodes across various roles — from system administrators and developers to auditors and users. These codes are valuable for enumeration, escalation, lateral movement, and general SAP landscape awareness. Use them to navigate, query, and manage key components of SAP systems.

techniques.What it do?: User management. Allows creating, modifying, locking, unlocking, or deleting user accounts. Often used by admins for identity operations.
Display or create custom TCodes. Used to map custom programs or ABAP reports to transaction codes. Useful for identifying hidden or custom logic.
Role maintenance. Manage roles and permissions. Crucial for privilege escalation or reviewing existing access rights.
Workload analysis. Used to view performance data and identify frequently used transactions or users. Good recon value.
RFC destination config. Lists external and internal SAP system links. Critical for lateral movement or pivoting across systems.
Object Navigator. Central hub for development activities — programs, classes, function modules. Devs live here.
Execute custom or standard ABAP programs. Often used to test or run logic on-the-fly — with access, can execute payloads.
Function module testing. Invoke SAP functions directly — useful for abuse or debugging RFC-enabled logic.
Dump analysis. Shows ABAP short dumps — can reveal sensitive program info or misconfigurations.
System log viewer. Displays OS-level and SAP system events. Great for spotting unusual activity or errors.
Deactivate TCodes. Used by admins to disable potentially dangerous or deprecated transactions.
Client administration. Define client settings like modifiability, remote access, and protections. Relevant for sandbox escape or transport abuse.
Background job monitor. Lets you review or schedule jobs. Useful for persistence or scheduled execution.
Table browser. Used to view DB table contents directly — from user tables to config entries. Goldmine for recon.
ICF Service config. Used to configure and view exposed web endpoints. Important for understanding the web attack surface.
System trace. Admin tool for tracing authorization checks, RFC calls, kernel calls, etc. Monitors what a user or process is doing.
DB monitoring. Lets you run SQL on the underlying DB if configured. Useful for direct data access or hash extraction.
SAP Project Reference Object. Entry point for customizing SAP system behavior. Massive config interface.
SAP directory listing. Shows server-side filesystem directories defined in the system. May leak paths or stored logs/files.
Standard text. Can be used to hide or review injected text/data in templates — often abused for data exfil.
